summary: Françoise Robin is a Tibetologist who earned her DEA at INALCO and completed her doctorate under Heather Stoddard. She directed the Tibetan department and Southeast Asia/Pacific department at INALCO, served as director at Collège de France, and founded SFEMT.

Fred Pfeil was a scholar in Buddhist studies and other fields who studied at Amherst College and Stanford University. He taught at Stanford, Stephens College, Oregon State University, and Trinity College, Hartford.
Freda Bedi worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She studied at St Hugh's College and under Mahasi Sayadaw, and founded the Young Lamas Home School and Karma Drubgyu Thargay Ling Nunnery.

Frederick James Furnivall was a linguist who studied at University College London and Trinity Hall, Cambridge. He co-founded the Philological Society, serving as its secretary, founded the Working Men's College and multiple literary societies, and edited the Oxford English Dictionary.
Frederick M. Asher was an Indologist and historian/archaeologist who served as a professor at the University of Minnesota from circa 1973 to 2021.
Frederick M. Smith is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who studied under Ludo Rocher. He served as a professor and later professor emeritus at the University of Iowa.

Frederick William Thomas was an Indologist and Tibetologist who studied at Cambridge under Edward Byles Cowell. He served as Assistant Librarian at the India Office, lectured at University College London and the University of London, and was Boden Professor at Oxford.

Frederik David Kan Bosch was an Indologist and archaeologist who studied under Jacob Samuel Speyer and Christianus Cornelis Uhlenbeck. He headed the Archaeological Service in the Dutch East Indies, followed by professorships at Utrecht University and Leiden University.

Fredrik Barth studied at the University of Chicago and Cambridge under Edmund Leach. He founded and held a professorship at the University of Bergen, later holding chairs and teaching posts at Oslo, the Museum of Cultural History, Emory, Harvard, and Boston University.

Friederike Assandri is a sinologist and scholar of religious studies who studied under Günther-Dietz Sontheimer and pursued doctoral studies at Heidelberg University, where she also held an attested post in 2013.

Friedhelm Hardy was an Indologist and religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Cologne and the University of Oxford. He served as Wilde Lecturer at Oxford and as Professor of Indian Religions at King's College London.

Friedrich Alexander Bischoff was a sinologist and Tibetologist who earned doctorates at the University of Paris under Marcelle Lalou and Robert des Rotours. He held professorships at Indiana University Bloomington, the University of Hamburg, and the University of Vienna.

Friedrich August Rosen was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Leipzig and under Franz Bopp in Berlin. He served as professor of Oriental languages and Sanskrit at the University of London (UCL) and held secretary roles in London scholarly societies.

Friedrich August Wolf was a linguist and historian who studied at the University of Göttingen under Christian Gottlob Heyne. He served on the faculty at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg from circa 1783 to 1806.

Friedrich Bechtel was a linguist and Indologist who studied under Theodor Benfey and August Fick at the University of Göttingen. He taught at Göttingen and served as ordinary professor of comparative linguistics at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg.

Friedrich Benedict Weber studied at the University of Leipzig and was an academic in political economy, holding posts at European University Viadrina and as professor at the University of Breslau from circa 1811 to 1848.

Friedrich Bollensen was a linguist and Indologist who studied Sanskrit under Heinrich Ewald at Göttingen. He served as adjunct professor at Saint Petersburg State University and Main Pedagogical Institute, and as ordinary professor of Sanskrit at Kazan State University.

Friedrich Brockhaus was a scholar who held professorships at the University of Basel (circa 1868–1871), the University of Jena (circa 1871–1872), Kiel University (circa 1872–1888), and the University of Marburg (circa 1888–1889).

Friedrich Carl Andreas was an Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar and linguist who studied at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg. He held academic posts at Humboldt University of Berlin and the University of Göttingen.
Friedrich Christian Diez was a linguist who studied at Giessen under Friedrich Gottlieb Welcker and at Göttingen. He served on the faculty at the University of Bonn from circa 1823 to 1876.
